# `kernel/execution/ExecutionApprovalMode.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/execution/ExecutionApprovalMode.js`

Deterministic execution-approval modes. This module decides whether an already-reviewed tool action still needs an operator prompt. It never grants authority: ToolActionReview, ToolRouter, Navi Faculty capability leases, workspace roots, and mounted-folder scopes remain authoritative for every call.

## Functions

### `normalizeExecutionApprovalMode(value)`

### `executionApprovalRepeatProfile(review, { appId = '', naviId = '' } = {})`

Content-free identity for a repeatable approval scope. Arguments are intentionally omitted: changed values may repeat only when the tool, descriptor, authority, data classes, and exact target scope are unchanged.

### `decideExecutionApproval({ mode, review, priorReceipt = null } = {})`

Decide only the prompt behavior for an action that has already passed the OS review. `priorReceipt` must be an OS-recorded successful call for the same repeat profile; model recommendations never substitute for it.

### `eligibleForVerifiedRepeat(review)`

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
